articles.headline: Vault heap‑view exposes AWS AgentCore token – what builders need to know
articles.dek: A default‑on AgentCore configuration combined with Vault’s experimental heap‑view leaks the instance token in cleartext, creating a low‑effort credential grab for attackers.

body.text: Key Takeaway

AWS’s AgentCore daemon ships with metadata exposure enabled by default, and Vault’s experimental heap‑view feature can dump that token in cleartext – a combination that gives attackers a ready‑made credential slice [FACT:57d866e5beff4d99aee8af8a3eab584f][FACT:1f4bf06c0bd16be0ea02c17239757a62].
Why This Matters

When you run AI inference containers on EC2, a stolen token lets an adversary impersonate the instance, read training data, or spin up rogue jobs because the token resides in memory before identity mapping finishes [FACT:57d866e5beff4d99aee8af8a3eab584f][FACT:5a57c3dc61d7c1d8ce237cd87fa798e5].
What Happened

Unit 42 found that Vault’s heap‑view, a debugging aid, copies the entire process heap to a temporary file. That file contains the AgentCore token in plaintext, exposing the bridge between the harness and the instance’s identity [FACT:1f4bf06c0bd16be0ea02c17239757a62][FACT:5a57c3dc61d7c1d8ce237cd87fa798e5].
Builder View

Builders should verify that AgentCore is not running with its default metadata exposure enabled and confirm that the heap‑view feature is disabled in production Vault deployments; both settings are part of the out‑of‑the‑box install and can be turned off to stop the clear‑text leak [FACT:57d866e5beff4d99aee8af8a3eab584f][FACT:1f4bf06c0bd16be0ea02c17239757a62].
Open Questions

Unit 42 highlighted open questions: how frequently heap‑view is instantiated in typical training jobs, whether future AgentCore releases will change the default metadata handling, and the performance impact of the hardening steps. These gaps have no published numbers yet [FACT:5a57c3dc61d7c1d8ce237cd87fa798e5].
Ardur Take

Two independent Unit 42 analyses converge on the same flaw, and both the AgentCore default behavior and Vault heap‑view findings are corroborated across sources, giving the report a high confidence rating [FACT:57d866e5beff4d99aee8af8a3eab584f][FACT:1f4bf06c0bd16be0ea02c17239757a62][FACT:5a57c3dc61d7c1d8ce237cd87fa798e5].

keyPoints: AgentCore’s default config leaves the instance metadata token exposed in memory [FACT:57d866e5beff4d99aee8af8a3eab584f].
Vault’s experimental heap‑view writes the full process heap, including the token, to disk in cleartext [FACT:1f4bf06c0bd16be0ea02c17239757a62].
Both findings are corroborated by two separate Unit 42 analyses, raising the severity for AI inference workloads [FACT:5a57c3dc61d7c1d8ce237cd87fa798e5].
articles.whyItMatters: AI workloads that depend on AWS compute resources now have a new credential‑exposure vector that can be exploited without needing to break encryption, directly threatening data confidentiality and model integrity.
articles.readerAction: Audit your EC2 instances for AgentCore metadata exposure and verify that Vault’s heap‑view feature is disabled in production; consider updating to hardened AMIs that disable the default token dump.

articles.headline: GitHub migrates Copilot runtime to Rust, using Copilot
articles.dek: GitHub rewrote the Copilot CLI agent in Rust, a move announced Sep 17 2026 that reshapes how builders run the tool in Kubernetes.

body.text: Key Takeaway

GitHub replaced the original TypeScript/Node Copilot agent with a Rust implementation, while the `gh copilot` command line stays the same. The rewrite was driven by a need to port the agent runtime to a language better suited for security, reliability and performance goals. [FACT:1cf635fbe44d5126e0bde757c812b311] [FACT:1a1e9d9d1400c77943c69582449ca158] [FACT:b6e4d7c6b1448bbe8af315ecd9f45e45]
Why This Matters

For Kubernetes and other cloud‑native workloads the Rust binary is smaller and runs without a Node runtime, which translates into lighter container images and fewer patched dependencies. That can simplify CI/CD pipelines and reduce the attack surface. [FACT:686953347e2777348cf05070b563a7ae] [FACT:b6e4d7c6b1448bbe8af315ecd9f45e45]
What Happened

On Sep 17 2026 GitHub published a blog post announcing the complete rewrite of the Copilot runtime in Rust, and a Microsoft engineer posted a follow‑up article describing the effort. The migration spanned 128 pull requests, with engineer Toub authoring the bulk of the code changes. [FACT:60b61338e888efaa4754c0fa6c929638] [FACT:a5da5450741b9d6379e2682ebdeb76c9] [FACT:c989b6cb0587ee86f1f92a25a5d2e3a6] [FACT:28eb2f4a718e07a677cb013331a5a35a]
Builder View

If you already use the `gh copilot` CLI in your Kubernetes pods, you can switch to the new Rust‑based image without altering any command‑line arguments; the interface and sub‑commands remain unchanged. The migration only affects the underlying runtime binary. [FACT:bfbbc81b111e77fe5ffa566348a25584] [FACT:1a1e9d9d1400c77943c69582449ca158]
Open Questions

The announcement focused on the open‑source CLI path, leaving the timing for the Rust binary to become the default in GitHub Enterprise installations unclear. Teams will need to monitor future GitHub communications for rollout details. [FACT:a5da5450741b9d6379e2682ebdeb76c9]
Ardur Take

Two independent sources confirm the scale and intent of the migration, and the facts line up cleanly. Confidence is high that the Rust runtime will become the primary agent for Copilot, and builders should start testing the new image in staging environments. [FACT:60b61338e888efaa4754c0fa6c929638] [FACT:4ac6b682f07b15ecd83f874e2e853705]

keyPoints: GitHub rewrote the Copilot agent from TypeScript/Node to Rust, keeping the CLI unchanged. [FACT:1cf635fbe44d5126e0bde757c812b311] [FACT:bfbbc81b111e77fe5ffa566348a25584]
The rewrite targets better security, reliability and performance. [FACT:b6e4d7c6b1448bbe8af315ecd9f45e45]
The effort involved 128 pull requests, with engineer Toub authoring most of the code. [FACT:c989b6cb0587ee86f1f92a25a5d2e3a6] [FACT:28eb2f4a718e07a677cb013331a5a35a]
The new Rust binary can run in Kubernetes without a Node runtime, shrinking container images. [FACT:686953347e2777348cf05070b563a7ae]
articles.whyItMatters: Kubernetes builders benefit from smaller, dependency‑free images and a runtime designed for security and performance, directly impacting CI/CD efficiency and cluster maintenance.
articles.readerAction: Pull the latest `gh copilot` Rust image, run your existing scripts in a test pod, and verify that the CLI behaves as before while observing resource usage.
